value.body: A two-year postgraduate nursing degree regulated by the Indian Nursing Council. Students specialise in one area — commonly medical-surgical, child health (paediatric), obstetric and gynaecological, community health, or mental health (psychiatric) nursing — and study nursing education, administration and research.

items.label: Course length
items.note: Includes clinical practice in the speciality and a research project

items.label: Regulator
items.note: Plus state nursing councils for registration

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Sc Nursing or Post Basic B.Sc Nursing (usually at least 55%), registration as a nurse (and midwife, for the OBG speciality) with a State Nursing Council, and normally at least one year of work experience. Admission is through entrance tests run by AIIMS, PGIMER, states or universities.

value.title: At a glance
items: It is the usual qualification for teaching posts in nursing colleges (tutor, lecturer and above).
It also leads to nurse educator, clinical specialist and nursing administration roles in hospitals.
A Ph.D in Nursing is the next step for senior academic posts.
